Use when asked to plan out, break down, or organize a multi-step project, research task, or any work requiring 5+ tool calls. Supports automatic session recovery after /clear.

teamily-bug-analysis
Bug Analysis skill for the Teamily product — root-cause analysis of errors and agent behavior. Activates when someone brings error logs, stack traces, exceptions, performance anomalies, or telemetry windows ("帮我看这段报错", "为什么登录变慢了", "这次发版后异常涨了吗", "analyze this error") — or agent-behavior problems ("agent 没回复/回复错了", "查 trace", "token 消耗异常", "为什么路由到了这个模型", "agent 工具调用失败", "analyze this trace") — or asks to turn findings into a filing-ready defect payload — or which bugs are still unresolved ("还没解决的", "哪些 bug 没修", "unresolved?") for an on-demand digest. Pulls PostHog telemetry and Langfuse agent-execution traces read-only, clusters exceptions by fingerprint, aligns anomalies with deploy versions and conversion funnels, and delivers responsive, standalone bilingual HTML reports with DEF payloads handed off to the bug-filing agent. Never files issues, never answers business-metric snapshot questions, never runs tests — those belong to bug-buddy, posthog-reader, and the QA Testing Agent.

Invoke at the start of Phase 2, before any AI-specific skill.
Add
architecture-design-ai
Use when designing any solution whose core value depends on an LLM or GenAI model — RAG systems, copilots, agents, AI-native features, semantic search, LLM-based generation/extraction/classification. Do not invoke for Traditional problems.
Add
ai-safety-guardrails
Use when designing safety, security, and governance for any LLM or GenAI application — prompt injection and jailbreak defense, hallucination control, content moderation, PII and secret leakage prevention, and data governance for prompts and logs. Invoke for every AI-centric or Hybrid solution; mandatory when the system retrieves untrusted content or calls tools.
Add
rag-knowledge-pipeline
Use when an AI solution must answer over private, proprietary, or frequently-changing data — enterprise knowledge bases, document Q&A, internal search, customer-support copilots grounded in company content. Covers ingestion, chunking, embedding choice, vector store selection, hybrid retrieval, reranking, freshness, and per-user access control on retrieved documents.
Add
adr-writing
Use when documenting or evaluating any significant technical decision — technology selection, architectural pattern choice, build-vs-buy, model or vendor selection. Provides the Architecture Decision Record format and the standard for what makes a decision defensible rather than merely asserted.
Add
region-compliance
Use when the target region, market, or user geography of a system is known or inferable, and the architecture must account for data privacy law, AI regulation, data residency, or regional vendor and model availability. Covers GDPR, PIPL, CCPA, LGPD, EU AI Act, cross-border transfer constraints, and how residency requirements shape topology.
Add
teamily-qa-testing
Unified QA Testing skill for the Teamily product — test design, regression execution, and release-gate verdicts in one self-contained, portable package. Activates when someone asks to design test cases for a feature/PRD/issue, run a smoke or regression, verify a fix, or judge whether a change is safe to ship ("能不能上线", "跑个回归", "test this", "release gate"). Cases are natural-language Markdown; execution goes through two sanctioned browser engines — the bundled generic visual-AI runner (Midscene + Puppeteer) or the platform's shell `ab` wrapper (agent-browser CLI) — no test-case code is ever written. Every verdict is backed by evidence (screenshots; redacted request/response logs for advisory non-browser rows) and passes mandatory self-check gates; gate verdicts are machine-bound to their coverage attestation.
Add
qa-html-deliverables-ca5871fa
Runs the Quality Gate on self-contained HTML deliverables (Teamily webpages) — JS syntax check, tag balance, HTTP 200 verification, and visual screenshot confirmation. Use when finishing or versioning any webpages/*/index.html deliverable, or when the user asks for a Quality Gate, JS syntax check, HTTP 200, visual screenshot, or visual check on a built page.
Add
spec-state-audit-0115fda0
Audit any screen, flow, form, or feature spec for the states, interaction details, and post-submission behavior it forgot to define. Use this whenever reviewing, critiquing, or completing a PRD, page spec, wireframe description, user flow, checkout or signup flow, or a design handoff — and also when writing one, to check it before delivering. Trigger on requests like "review this spec", "did I miss anything", "is this ready for engineering", "audit this flow", or any spec that describes what happens when things go right without saying what happens when they go wrong. Do not use for visual design critique or copywriting.
Add
kill-criteria-0115fda0
Write falsifiable stop conditions for any plan, roadmap, experiment, campaign, initiative, or investment — the specific metric, threshold, observation window, and action that would end the work. Use this whenever a plan, phased rollout, pilot, test, budget allocation, or strategy is being drafted or reviewed, and whenever someone asks "how will we know if this is working", "when should we cut this", "what does success look like", or presents success criteria without stop criteria. Also use it to fix vague stop conditions like "if users don't like it" into something that can actually trigger. Do not use for personal decisions or for post-hoc explanation of outcomes.
Add
rice-degradation-0115fda0
Prioritize a list of requirements, features, projects, campaigns, or investments with RICE scoring when the input data is incomplete — including the degradation paths for missing reach numbers, unestimated effort, and low confidence, plus override rules that outrank the score. Use this whenever someone asks what to build or do first, presents a backlog or wishlist to rank, asks "is this worth doing", or wants a roadmap ordered — and especially when they have not supplied clean numbers, which is almost always. Do not use when the data is complete and the answer is a straight arithmetic sort; do it directly instead.
Add
research-synthesis
从用户研究证据中提炼命名产物——Persona(用户画像)、User Journey(用户旅程)、使用场景、痛点与需求清单、需求优先级。Synthesize named research deliverables from evidence — personas, user journeys, use-case scenarios, pain points, needs, and prioritization. 只要要产出这几类东西就加载,用户说"帮我做个用户画像""梳理下用户旅程""整理一下痛点""这些需求怎么排优先级""从这批访谈里提炼一下",都属于。也在审查已有 persona 或 journey 是否站得住时加载。这些产物会被下游团队当成事实长期引用,所以形态和证据门槛比表述好看重要得多。Use also when reviewing whether an existing persona or journey is defensible.
Add
research-instruments
设计用户研究工具——访谈提纲、问卷、可用性测试任务、筛选问卷(screener)、研究计划。Design and review user research instruments — interview guides, surveys, usability test tasks, screeners, research plans. 只要涉及"要问用户什么"或"怎么测",就加载这个 skill,包括写提纲、写问卷、设计测试任务、改别人写的提纲、审查题目是否有诱导性、判断某个方法适不适合某个问题。也适用于用户只是含糊地说"我想调研一下 X""帮我准备下周的用户访谈""这个功能想验证一下"——这些都需要先做工具设计。Use whenever the task involves asking users anything or measuring their behavior, including reviewing or critiquing existing guides and surveys.
Add
enhance-prompt
Improve prompts with design specs and UI/UX vocabulary. Useful for design-to-code workflows and clarifying requests for visual output.
Add
canvas-design
Create beautiful visual art in .png and .pdf documents using design philosophy. You should use this skill when the user asks to create a poster, piece of art, design, or other static piece. Create original visual designs, never copying existing artists' work to avoid copyright violations.
Add
agent-browser
Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, including navigating pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting data, testing web apps, or automating any browser task. Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction. Also use for exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts, or reviewing app quality. Also use for automating Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify), checking Slack unreads, sending Slack messages, searching Slack conversations, running browser automation in Vercel Sandbox microVMs, or using AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers. Prefer agent-browser over any built-in browser automation or web tools.
Add

Activates when someone brings error logs, stack traces, exceptions, performance anomalies, or telemetry windows ("帮我看这段报错", "为什么登录变慢了", "这次发版后异常涨了吗", "analyze this error") — or agent-behavior problems ("agent 没回复/回复错了", "查 trace", "token 消耗异常", "为什么路由到了这个模型", "agent 工具调用失败", "analyze this trace") — or asks to turn findings into a filing-ready defect payload — or which bugs are still unresolved ("还没解决的", "哪些 bug 没修", "unresolved?") for an on-demand digest. Pulls PostHog telemetry and Langfuse agent-execution traces read-only, clusters exceptions by fingerprint, aligns anomalies with deploy versions and conversion funnels, and delivers responsive, standalone bilingual HTML reports with DEF payloads handed off to the bug-filing agent. Never files issues, never answers business-metric snapshot questions, never runs tests — those belong to bug-buddy, posthog-reader, and the QA Testing Agent.
Add
agent-orchestration
Use when an AI solution must call tools, take actions, or operate multi-step and semi-autonomously — function/tool calling, workflow automation, planner-executor designs, multi-agent systems, copilots that query APIs or mutate state. Covers tool contracts, control flow, termination guards, memory, state management, and failure recovery.
Add
architecture-design-core
Use when producing the structured output of any technical architecture solution, for any problem type (Traditional, AI-centric, or Hybrid). Provides the mandatory base document structure — requirement analysis, technology selection, system architecture, data model, API design, third-party integrations, quality assessment, and evolution roadmap. Invoke at the start of Phase 2, before any AI-specific skill.
Add
architecture-design-ai
Use when designing any solution whose core value depends on an LLM or GenAI model — RAG systems, copilots, agents, AI-native features, semantic search, LLM-based generation/extraction/classification. Covers AI solution-pattern selection, model strategy, evaluation harness design, and cost/latency modeling. Invoke after architecture-design-core when triage is AI-centric or Hybrid. Do not invoke for Traditional problems.
Add
ai-safety-guardrails
Use when designing safety, security, and governance for any LLM or GenAI application — prompt injection and jailbreak defense, hallucination control, content moderation, PII and secret leakage prevention, and data governance for prompts and logs. Invoke for every AI-centric or Hybrid solution; mandatory when the system retrieves untrusted content or calls tools.
Add
rag-knowledge-pipeline
Use when an AI solution must answer over private, proprietary, or frequently-changing data — enterprise knowledge bases, document Q&A, internal search, customer-support copilots grounded in company content. Covers ingestion, chunking, embedding choice, vector store selection, hybrid retrieval, reranking, freshness, and per-user access control on retrieved documents.
Add
adr-writing
Use when documenting or evaluating any significant technical decision — technology selection, architectural pattern choice, build-vs-buy, model or vendor selection. Provides the Architecture Decision Record format and the standard for what makes a decision defensible rather than merely asserted.
Add
region-compliance
Use when the target region, market, or user geography of a system is known or inferable, and the architecture must account for data privacy law, AI regulation, data residency, or regional vendor and model availability. Covers GDPR, PIPL, CCPA, LGPD, EU AI Act, cross-border transfer constraints, and how residency requirements shape topology.
Add
teamily-qa-testing
Unified QA Testing skill for the Teamily product — test design, regression execution, and release-gate verdicts in one self-contained, portable package. Activates when someone asks to design test cases for a feature/PRD/issue, run a smoke or regression, verify a fix, or judge whether a change is safe to ship ("能不能上线", "跑个回归", "test this", "release gate"). Cases are natural-language Markdown; execution goes through two sanctioned browser engines — the bundled generic visual-AI runner (Midscene + Puppeteer) or the platform's shell `ab` wrapper (agent-browser CLI) — no test-case code is ever written. Every verdict is backed by evidence (screenshots; redacted request/response logs for advisory non-browser rows) and passes mandatory self-check gates; gate verdicts are machine-bound to their coverage attestation.
Add
qa-html-deliverables-ca5871fa
Runs the Quality Gate on self-contained HTML deliverables (Teamily webpages) — JS syntax check, tag balance, HTTP 200 verification, and visual screenshot confirmation. Use when finishing or versioning any webpages/*/index.html deliverable, or when the user asks for a Quality Gate, JS syntax check, HTTP 200, visual screenshot, or visual check on a built page.
Add
spec-state-audit-0115fda0
Audit any screen, flow, form, or feature spec for the states, interaction details, and post-submission behavior it forgot to define. Use this whenever reviewing, critiquing, or completing a PRD, page spec, wireframe description, user flow, checkout or signup flow, or a design handoff — and also when writing one, to check it before delivering. Trigger on requests like "review this spec", "did I miss anything", "is this ready for engineering", "audit this flow", or any spec that describes what happens when things go right without saying what happens when they go wrong. Do not use for visual design critique or copywriting.
Add
kill-criteria-0115fda0
Write falsifiable stop conditions for any plan, roadmap, experiment, campaign, initiative, or investment — the specific metric, threshold, observation window, and action that would end the work. Use this whenever a plan, phased rollout, pilot, test, budget allocation, or strategy is being drafted or reviewed, and whenever someone asks "how will we know if this is working", "when should we cut this", "what does success look like", or presents success criteria without stop criteria. Also use it to fix vague stop conditions like "if users don't like it" into something that can actually trigger. Do not use for personal decisions or for post-hoc explanation of outcomes.
Add
rice-degradation-0115fda0
Prioritize a list of requirements, features, projects, campaigns, or investments with RICE scoring when the input data is incomplete — including the degradation paths for missing reach numbers, unestimated effort, and low confidence, plus override rules that outrank the score. Use this whenever someone asks what to build or do first, presents a backlog or wishlist to rank, asks "is this worth doing", or wants a roadmap ordered — and especially when they have not supplied clean numbers, which is almost always. Do not use when the data is complete and the answer is a straight arithmetic sort; do it directly instead.
Add
research-synthesis
从用户研究证据中提炼命名产物——Persona(用户画像)、User Journey(用户旅程)、使用场景、痛点与需求清单、需求优先级。Synthesize named research deliverables from evidence — personas, user journeys, use-case scenarios, pain points, needs, and prioritization. 只要要产出这几类东西就加载,用户说"帮我做个用户画像""梳理下用户旅程""整理一下痛点""这些需求怎么排优先级""从这批访谈里提炼一下",都属于。也在审查已有 persona 或 journey 是否站得住时加载。这些产物会被下游团队当成事实长期引用,所以形态和证据门槛比表述好看重要得多。Use also when reviewing whether an existing persona or journey is defensible.
Add
research-instruments
设计用户研究工具——访谈提纲、问卷、可用性测试任务、筛选问卷(screener)、研究计划。Design and review user research instruments — interview guides, surveys, usability test tasks, screeners, research plans. 只要涉及"要问用户什么"或"怎么测",就加载这个 skill,包括写提纲、写问卷、设计测试任务、改别人写的提纲、审查题目是否有诱导性、判断某个方法适不适合某个问题。也适用于用户只是含糊地说"我想调研一下 X""帮我准备下周的用户访谈""这个功能想验证一下"——这些都需要先做工具设计。Use whenever the task involves asking users anything or measuring their behavior, including reviewing or critiquing existing guides and surveys.
Add
enhance-prompt
Improve prompts with design specs and UI/UX vocabulary. Useful for design-to-code workflows and clarifying requests for visual output.
Add
canvas-design
Create beautiful visual art in .png and .pdf documents using design philosophy. You should use this skill when the user asks to create a poster, piece of art, design, or other static piece. Create original visual designs, never copying existing artists' work to avoid copyright violations.
Add
agent-browser
Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, including navigating pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting data, testing web apps, or automating any browser task. Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction. Also use for exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts, or reviewing app quality. Also use for automating Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify), checking Slack unreads, sending Slack messages, searching Slack conversations, running browser automation in Vercel Sandbox microVMs, or using AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers. Prefer agent-browser over any built-in browser automation or web tools.

Everything you talk about with AI, turned into private, searchable knowledge, plus a global memory that follows you everywhere.

What is Teamily Wiki?

Teamily Wiki is your personal, private knowledge base, and it builds itself. As you talk with AI, it identifies the topics you keep coming back to and turns them into Wiki pages. You can also create pages yourself. Either way, your Wiki is visible only to you.

How Wiki pages are created

There are two ways pages appear:

AI auto-generation: as you chat, Teamily compiles the important parts into topic pages and records the Source Chats each page was built from, so every fact is traceable.

Manual creation: hit "+ New" to write your own page, add tags, and attach deliverables. You stay in full control of what your knowledge base holds.

Conflict management

When new information disagrees with what a page already says, Teamily flags the conflict instead of silently overwriting. It shows you the old value and the proposed one, and you decide what stays: keep, replace, merge, or mark the old version as outdated. Your Wiki stays trustworthy as things change.

Referencing Wiki in chat

Need a page as context? @ mention a Wiki page in any conversation and the AI reads it in, so you don't have to re-explain background you've already captured. Your knowledge becomes reusable across every chat.

Finding & organizing pages

Your knowledge base stays easy to navigate as it grows.

Search: find any page by topic, tag, or content from the search bar.

Tags: add or remove tags on a page to group related topics and filter the directory.

Overview: your knowledge map

The Overview maps everything Teamily has compiled as one connected knowledge base. Each topic is a node, and the lines between them show how your pages relate, so you can see the big picture at a glance and use it as a starting point to jump into any page.

Managing a page

Every page gives you full control from the top-right actions:

Version history: view past versions of a page and restore an earlier one whenever you need.

Download: export a page (and its attached deliverables) to keep or share outside Teamily.

Delete: remove a page you no longer need; your knowledge base is always yours to curate.

This investment research report provides a pre-institutional assessment of 'Atlas AI,' an enterprise AI customer-support agent company. It evaluates the company's financial profile, including $23M ARR, 72% gross margin, and 118% net revenue retention, against a $180M pre-money valuation. The report features a comprehensive financial analysis, a detailed competitive landscape mapping against key players, and an examination of structural risks within the crowded AI agent market. It outlines key investment risks, thesis breakers, and seven specific due diligence questions with good/bad answer tests. A critical finding highlights the lack of public evidence for a company matching Atlas AI's description and a significant name-collision risk, leading to a recommendation to proceed to diligence with low conviction. All figures related to Atlas AI are flagged as unverified, emphasizing the need for thorough verification before any investment.

# Web Development

Design, build, and reliably deliver web pages that render correctly and return a shareable link. The hard part of web delivery is not writing HTML — it is guaranteeing the *published* page renders with every asset intact. This skill encodes that discipline.

## When to use this skill

- Create a new website, landing page, portfolio, dashboard, or documentation site
- Redesign or restyle an existing page
- Recreate ("clone") a page from a reference URL, then customize it
- Produce a new version of a page you previously built
- Audit and fix a page that renders blank, has broken images, or dead links

## Tools this skill uses

| Tool | Used for |
|------|----------|
| `create_file` | Write the initial `index.html` / CSS / JS into the project folder |
| `edit_file` | **The mandatory editor.** AI-applied edits using `// ... existing code ...` markers around the changed lines |
| `str_replace` | Surgical single-occurrence replacement when `edit_file` is overkill |
| `full_file_rewrite` | Replace an entire file (last resort, or template-slide rewrites) |
| `execute_command` | Download assets, run the quality-gate checks, `node --check` JS |
| `image_search` | Find topic-specific imagery (batch: `query=["…","…"]`, `num_results`) |
| `image_edit_or_generate` | Generate custom imagery/logos (`mode="generate"`) |
| `ab_navigate` / `ab_screenshot` / `ab_exec` | Drive a real browser for the Visual Check |
| `understand_image` | Read a screenshot back to confirm the page rendered correctly |

## File organization (non-negotiable)

A correct directory layout is what makes assets resolve after publishing.

- Every page project lives in its own folder: `create_file("webpages/<project>/index.html", …)`. Never write a bare `index.html` at the workspace root — it collides with other tasks and is not persisted.
- All images/media go in `webpages/<project>/images/` and are referenced **relatively** in HTML (`images/hero.jpg`). Files outside the project folder are dropped at publish time.
- Names must match `^[a-z0-9_-]+$` — lowercase, hyphen/underscore only, no spaces or non-ASCII.

## Editing discipline

- **One file per request.*

# Skill Creator

A skill for creating new skills and iteratively improving them.

At a high level, the process of creating a skill goes like this:

- Decide what you want the skill to do and roughly how it should do it
- Write a draft of the skill
- Create a few test prompts and run claude-with-access-to-the-skill on them
- Help the user evaluate the results both qualitatively and quantitatively
  - While the runs happen in the background, draft some quantitative evals if there aren't any (if there are some, you can either use as is or modify if you feel something needs to change about them). Then explain them to the user (or if they already existed, explain the ones that already exist)
  - Use the `eval-viewer/generate_review.py` script to show the user the results for them to look at, and also let them look at the quantitative metrics
- Rewrite the skill based on feedback from the user's evaluation of the results (and also if there are any glaring flaws that become apparent from the quantitative benchmarks)
- Repeat until you're satisfied
- Expand the test set and try again at larger scale

Your job when using this skill is to figure out where the user is in this process and then jump in and help them progress through these stages. So for instance, maybe they're like "I want to make a skill for X". You can help narrow down what they mean, write a draft, write the test cases, figure out how they want to evaluate, run all the prompts, and repeat.

On the other hand, maybe they already have a draft of the skill. In this case you can go straight to the eval/iterate part of the loop.

Of course, you should always be flexible and if the user is like "I don't need to run a bunch of evaluations, just vibe with me", you can do that instead.

Then after the skill is done (but again, the order is flexible), you can also run the skill description improver, which we have a whole separate script for, to optimize the triggering of the skill.

Cool? Cool.

## Communicating with the user

The skill creator is liable to be used by people across a wide range of familiarity with coding jargon. If you haven't heard (and how could you, it's only very recently that it started), there's a trend now where the power of Claude is inspiring plumbers to open up their terminals, parents and grandparents to google "how to install npm". On the other hand, the bulk of users are probably fairly computer-literate.

So please pay attention to context cues to understand how to phrase your communication! In the default case, just to give you some idea:

- "evaluation" and "benchmark" are borderline, but OK
- for "JSON" and "assertion" you want to see serious cues from the user that they know what those things are before using them without explaining them

{"page_id":"d98d29fe-6283-472f-a3a6-cc6fb4fe4dea","account_id":"2e9d0c35-d2e6-45e9-bde1-ac0cb00bb878","title":"Teamily Wiki: Your Personal Knowledge Base","summary":"How your private wiki builds itself from chats, handles conflicts, and can be referenced anywhere.","content":"Everything you talk about with AI, turned into private, searchable knowledge, plus a global memory that follows you everywhere.

## What is Teamily Wiki?

Teamily Wiki is your personal, private knowledge base, and it builds itself. As you talk with AI, it identifies the topics you keep coming back to and turns them into Wiki pages. You can also create pages yourself. Either way, your Wiki is visible only to you.

## How Wiki pages are created

There are two ways pages appear:

- **AI auto-generation**: as you chat, Teamily compiles the important parts into topic pages and records the Source Chats each page was built from, so every fact is traceable.
- **Manual creation**: hit "+ New" to write your own page, add tags, and attach deliverables. You stay in full control of what your knowledge base holds.

## Conflict management

When new information disagrees with what a page already says, Teamily flags the conflict instead of silently overwriting. It shows you the old value and the proposed one, and you decide what stays: keep, replace, merge, or mark the old version as outdated. Your Wiki stays trustworthy as things change.

## Referencing Wiki in chat

Need a page as context? @ mention a Wiki page in any conversation and the AI reads it in, so you don't have to re-explain background you've already captured. Your knowledge becomes reusable across every chat.

## Finding & organizing pages

Your knowledge base stays easy to navigate as it grows.

- **Search**: find any page by topic, tag, or content from the search bar.
- **Tags**: add or remove tags on a page to group related topics and filter the directory.

## Overview: your knowledge map

The Overview maps everything Teamily has compiled as one connected knowledge base. Each topic is a node, and the lines between them show how your pages relate, so you can see the big picture at a glance and use it as a starting point to jump into any page.

## Managing a page

Every page gives you full control from the top-right actions:

- **Version history**: view past versions of a page and restore an earlier one whenever you need.
- **Download**: export a page (and its attached deliverables) to keep or share outside Teamily.

## 🧠 Your Identity & Memory

You are **Quinn**, a veteran Investment Researcher with 14+ years across buy-side equity research, venture capital due diligence, and institutional asset management. Your superpower is asking the questions that everyone else missed and finding the data that challenges the comfortable narrative.

**You remember and carry forward:**
- The bull case is always easy to write. Spend more time on the bear case — that's where the risk hides.

Produce institutional-quality investment research that surfaces actionable insights, quantifies risks and opportunities, and supports data-driven portfolio decisions. Ensure every investment thesis is supported by rigorous analysis, clearly stated assumptions, identifiable catalysts, and well-defined risk factors.

## 🚨 Critical Rules You Must Follow

1. **Separate thesis from narrative.** A compelling story isn't an investment thesis. Every thesis needs quantifiable support, testable predictions, and identifiable catalysts.
2. **Always present both sides.** The bull case and bear case must be equally rigorous. Advocacy without balance is marketing, not research.
3. **Cite primary sources.** SEC filings, earnings transcripts, industry data, and patent filings. Not blog posts, not social media, not sell-side summaries.
4. **Quantify the downside.** Every investment recommendation must include a downside scenario with specific loss estimates. "It could go down" is not a risk assessment.
5. **Define the investment horizon.** A 6-month trade and a 5-year investment require completely different analysis frameworks. Be explicit.
6. **Disclose your confidence level.** High-conviction ideas vs. speculative positions require different sizing. State your conviction
